@graph.name: corpus-grep
@graph.title: Corpus-Grep Skill
@graph.description: Pre-declaration corpus check. Before declaring any item "open", "gap", "TODO", "open problem", "pending derivation" — or asserting in chat that something is unresolved in the corpus — run the four-path grep checklist. A source file's `## Status` note lags the corpus by weeks; the corpus is the source of truth. An item is open only after all four paths come back empty (modulo the originating file itself).

@graph.name: chapter-complexity-review
@graph.title: Chapter Complexity Review
@graph.description: Analyse a chapter's internal dependency graph to find backward edges (blocks that reference something defined later), compute graph energy, and suggest section/block reorderings that minimise complexity. Uses Graphviz for visualisation and brute-force permutation search for optimal section ordering.

@graph.name: swarm-management
@graph.title: Swarm management
@graph.description: Decide whether to run parallel agents at all, and if so how many, at which model level, against which decomposition. Read BEFORE dispatching more than one background agent — a swarm spends the author's tokens and the decision is theirs.

@graph.name: watch
@graph.title: /watch — background watcher with integration check
@graph.description: Background-watch a branch (default origin/main) or a GitHub PR for new activity while you work, and on every event report whether to integrate / whether it conflicts with the current branch / whether it lets you simplify exposition / proofs / computations

@graph.name: canonical-watcher
@graph.title: /canonical-watcher
@graph.description: Derivation-discipline integration watcher — watches the default branch + open active PRs + newly-opened PRs for non-canonical empirical / fitting / calibration inputs beyond the project's declared set, numerology, or justification/rationalization in place of derivation. Inherits shared mechanics (Monitor, subscriptions, queue, ledger, idle sweep, author-ask, watch-prepared-PRs, witness-drift recovery, billing-quick-fail flake, post-completion one-voice, sibling-PR comment protocol, backlog-found PR spin-up, handover docs) from `local/integration-watcher`.

@graph.name: bib-human-review
@graph.title: bib-human-review
@graph.description: Human-validated bibliography workflow. Flag references that have not been human-reviewed against their source; drive the acquisition ladder (source-in-repo → acquire-legally → physical-library); open one GitHub issue per reference needing physical review (full project context + bibliographic data + page-photo request, assigned to the repo owner); hand off uploaded photos to the bib-photo-ingestion watcher. Use when auditing bib human-review status, ingesting an uploaded paper's results, or preparing a physical-review issue.

@graph.name: process-state
@graph.title: Process state — the task you are in, inside the process you are running
@graph.description: Track where you are inside a running process — which task, in which swimlane, under which role — and recover deliberately when you find yourself outside it. Read before completing a workflow step, and whenever something unexpected interrupts one.

@graph.name: detangler-integration-watcher
@graph.title: /detangler-integration-watcher
@graph.description: Structural-QA integration watcher — watches the default branch + open active PRs + newly-opened PRs for organisational changes (paper / chapter manifest edits, new blocks, edited `uses[]` / `kind` / `label` / `interprets` / `defines` / `tags`, block renames) and runs the editor's detanglement skill suite (`content-graph`, `chapter-complexity-review`, `block-density`, `critical-path-analysis`) on every detected change. Queues findings, auto-discharges mechanical fixes (table extraction), routes block reorderings through narrative review before applying them, and escalates section splits / merges / cross-chapter moves / new sections to the author. Inherits shared mechanics from `local/integration-watcher`.

@graph.name: compute-integration-watcher
@graph.title: Compute Integration Watcher
@graph.description: Cross-layer wiring auditor — watches for newly-landed formal/analytic improvements (proofs, propositions, lemmas, axiom→theorem upgrades, witness data) on the default branch AND on open PRs, and checks whether each one has been wired into the production compute chain. Complements `local/compute-audit` (which scans for performance/correctness antipatterns inside scripts). Runs in two modes: REACTIVE (watch new commits / PR events) and IDLE-SWEEP (walk all existing content blocks and audit wiring).

@graph.name: one-voice-style-guide
@graph.title: One-Voice Style Guide — Author Voice Profile
@graph.description: Author voice profile and narrative style guide. Reference when authoring or editing prose. Pairs with `one-voice-audit` (mechanical sweep for status leaks, emoji, and Unicode crashes).

@graph.name: integration-watch
@graph.title: /integration-watch — dispatcher for the integration watchers
@graph.description: Dispatcher for the `/integration-watch` slash command. Routes to one or more of the concrete integration watchers / audits (proof, canonical, compute, detangler, one-voice, consolidation, bibliography, devils-advocate, …). With no argument, lists the available watchers and asks the user which to invoke. With arguments, dispatches the named watchers in parallel (each gets its own Monitor, queue, ledger, and PR-subscription set).

@graph.name: skills-and-tools
@graph.title: Skills and Tools — the skill says what, the Tool says how
@graph.description: A skill states a capability generically; a Tool node carries the concrete mechanism. Read before writing or editing any skill, and whenever a skill is about to name a vendor, a CLI, a binary or an API endpoint.

@graph.name: uses-editorial-review
@graph.title: `uses[]` Editorial Review
@graph.description: Adjudicate `uses-editorial-completeness` — read a block as a reader would and judge whether its `uses[]` is complete and genuinely expository.  The human/agent half of the `uses` QA axis; the mechanical half runs in `qa-checkers-uses.ts`.

@graph.name: repo-conversion
@graph.title: /repo-conversion — folio-assistant over a repo that already has a life
@graph.description: Lay folio-assistant over a repository that already exists, without losing or silently moving what is in it. Scans the tree read-only, classifies candidate files into library (external source) and content (authored here) with an explicit third bucket for what it cannot classify, puts the three questions the scan cannot answer to the author as selections, and hands ingestion to one agent or a small swarm. Use when a user wants an existing repo converted to a folio, asks to import what is already there, or asks whether their PDFs/notes/drafts can come along.

@graph.name: mcp-projection
@graph.title: MCP projection — turning a Tool node into an MCP service
@graph.description: Generate an MCP server from Tool nodes — the mapping from this harness's skill/Tool vocabulary onto the current MCP standard. Read before exposing a CLI tool over MCP, or when asked how an agent stands a service up.

@graph.name: todo-review
@graph.title: Todo Review Skill
@graph.description: Monitor and triage open feedback across all content blocks. At session start, ask the author if they'd like to work on feedback. Provide overview, let them pick a chapter/section, then review and iterate until done.

@graph.name: devils-advocate-watcher
@graph.title: /devils-advocate-watcher
@graph.description: Logical devil's-advocate integration watcher — for every content block (.ts/.md) and formal sibling, constructs the strongest adversarial case that it is WRONG: the objection a hostile-but- competent referee would raise (false claim, vacuity, circularity, overclaim, hidden degree-of-freedom, logical non-sequitur, formal↔narrative divergence, citation misuse, definitional ambiguity, empirical fragility, domain implausibility, irreproducible compute). Fans out multiple adversarial-lens agents per block, then an adjudicator scores whether each objection survives rebuttal. Persists per-block <block>.qa.json entries under the `da-*` criteria family (reviewer.kind = "agent"). Operationalizes the standing Critical-distance red-team license (AGENTS.md). Inherits all shared mechanics (Monitor, subscriptions, queue, ledger, idle sweep, author-ask, watch-prepared-PRs, witness-drift recovery, billing-quick-fail flake) from `integration-watcher`.

@graph.name: diff
@graph.title: Diff — Content Block Change Report
@graph.description: Show per-block content changes with viewer links, changelog, and undo impact analysis

@graph.name: continual-progress
@graph.title: /continual-progress — trackable, always-PR'd, continually-committed work
@graph.description: Make in-flight work trackable by others in real time — open a PR from the first commit, push small coherent increments continuously (never hoard uncommitted work), keep a live status checklist in the PR body, and post brief intent on the PR + any overlapping sibling PRs. Use on any multi-step or long-running task, especially when siblings/agents or the author may need to follow, cherry-pick, or take over mid-flight.

@graph.name: docs-generation
@graph.title: Documentation Generation Skill
@graph.description: Generate and deploy documentation artifacts: schema docs (TypeDoc), formal-layer API docs, dependency graphs, schema manifests, and per-paper HTML/PDF/Markdown outputs.

@graph.name: directory-conventions
@graph.title: Directory conventions — what an instance declares it scans

@graph.name: getting-started
@graph.title: /getting-started — what did they actually ask for?
@graph.description: Triage what a person means when they ask to create a folio, and route them. Five requests share one sentence — a folio in a new repo, folio-assistant overlaid on an existing repo, a second folio in an instance that already has one, a content object they called a folio, or something the filesystem cannot tell apart. Reads the repository facts, runs them through the folio-intent decision table, asks a selectable question for what facts cannot settle, scaffolds, and reports the published URL. Use whenever a user asks to create, start, set up, or initialise a folio, a paper, a DAK, an IG, or "folio-assistant" itself.

@graph.name: interaction-modality
@graph.title: /interaction-modality — ask in a form the person can answer
@graph.description: Establish how to talk to the person in front of you before deciding what to say — audio, ordinary chat, selectable options for limited hand function, large-type for low vision, plain language — and hold that choice durably so every later session and sibling agent honours it. Covers the accessibility rules a conversational agent can actually keep, the settings surface in the published site, and how to drive a question set from DMN so the SAME logic serves every modality. Use at first contact with a new user, when a user reports difficulty answering, whenever a question is about to be asked, and before any long free-text prompt.

@graph.name: delivery-summary
@graph.title: Delivery Summary
@graph.description: Post-delivery summary with server restart command and viewer links

@graph.name: bean-coordination
@graph.title: Bean Coordination
@graph.description: Pointer to the bean-based session work-plan system (the `beans` CLI flat-file issue tracker, data under `beans/`). Operational usage lives in todo-manager.md / session-intent.md; the generic coordinator/orchestrator logic is owned by the folio-assistant platform.

@graph.name: dispatch-agent
@graph.title: /dispatch-agent — parallel dispatch with a live 2-minute status heartbeat
@graph.description: Dispatch one or more background sub-agents against parallel research/build fronts with a STANDARDIZED live progress contract, and monitor them on a 2-minute heartbeat. Every dispatched agent emits consistent DID/DOING/NEXT/BLOCKERS blocks with real log output (not static "still running"); the parent extracts the latest block from each agent every ~120 s and posts one consolidated synthesis table. Use when the user says "dispatch agents", "fan out", "run these in parallel with monitoring", "give me status every 2 minutes", or when you are about to launch ≥ 2 background Agents on independent work.

@graph.name: feature-staging
@graph.title: Feature-branch staging
@graph.description: Manages feature-branch staging deployments under gh-pages/STAGING/<branch-slug>/ for before/after publication review comparison. Handles branch creation, staging deployment, commit SHA stamping, and cleanup.

@graph.name: production-vs-exploratory-discipline
@graph.title: Production vs exploratory vs numerology — the bright-line guide
@graph.description: Distinguish PRODUCTION (derived-only, no fits) from EXPLORATORY (empirical-fit probes OK as shape-hints) from NUMEROLOGY (post-hoc fits to known constants). The hidden-extra-input / empirical-fit antipattern is a common review-churn source: agents promote empirical fits into production scripts, "closed" status, dashboards, and named constants without a derivation. This skill is the bright-line guide for which output goes where, the derivation-menu check, and the escalation path for off-menu coefficients.

@graph.name: translation-manager
@graph.title: Translation manager
@graph.description: Translation lifecycle management for folio content. Covers gettext PO/POT extraction and injection, TranslationNode manifests as KG nodes, official vs unofficial translations, staleness tracking, sign-off workflow, automatic badge rendering, and the poSources fallback resolution chain.

@graph.name: integration-audit
@graph.title: /integration-audit — invalidate + re-audit the sidecar pipeline
@graph.description: Sidecar-invalidation utility for the integration-watcher pipeline. Adds mechanical QA fields (script-reviewer entries) to per-block `.qa.json` sidecars and marks the existing entries stale so the next `qa-sweep` re-evaluates them. Use when a checker bug is fixed in a QA checker module (downstream "fresh" entries are now incorrect) or when a registry update adds a criterion the block hasn't been audited under.

@graph.name: ontologist
@graph.title: Semantic Ontologist (Ambiguity Detection & Glossary)
@graph.description: Semantic Ontologist — scans narrative text for ambiguous terms, generates a formal glossary/registry, and produces a mapping linking narrative strings to formal identifiers. Acts as the "Gatekeeper" ensuring every term has a unique type/identity assignment before formalization proceeds.

@graph.name: pickup
@graph.title: Pickup Skill
@graph.description: Pick up / continue work on one or more existing open PRs efficiently. Resolves each PR's REAL branch + title + checklist + reviews + CI in one batched pass, classifies CI as billing-vs-real, then dispatches one worktree sub-agent per PR with a filled-in brief, and applies the safe class of review-nit fixes (eval→ast.literal_eval, dead-code/unused-var removal, etc.). Use when the user says "pick up PR N", "continue 1543/1576/1571", "work these PRs", "address the review on PR N", or "take over PR N".

@graph.name: kg-export
@graph.title: KG export — publishing the graph as data, not as a page
@graph.description: Serialize an instance's knowledge graph to one JSON document, for publication and inspection. Read when asked to visualize, audit or share the KG, and before adding a node type to the export.

@graph.name: todo-manager
@graph.title: Session Task Manager (`beans`)
@graph.description: Maintain and display work-in-progress task lists using the `beans` CLI issue tracker. Track implementation progress, open tasks, missing artifacts, and blocked items across a session.

@graph.name: mcp-assembly
@graph.title: MCP assembly — many Tools, one service, one namespace
@graph.description: Compose several Tool nodes into one MCP service — naming, collisions, grouping and versioning. Read when a service will expose more than one tool, or when two instances' tools land in the same namespace.

@graph.name: staging-review
@graph.title: Staging review — before/after comparison
@graph.description: Staging preview and before/after comparison for content review. Provides before (MAIN) and after (STAGING) URLs for rendered content so reviewers can visually compare changes. Used by CRDM feature development workflow and content authoring review sessions.

@graph.name: mcp-contract
@graph.title: MCP contract — the projected service must match what it was projected from
@graph.description: Verify an MCP service's tools against the Tool nodes and skill declarations they came from — I/O equivalence in both directions. Read before shipping a projected server, and when a tool call fails with an argument the schema said was fine.

@graph.name: bib-photo-ingestion-watcher
@graph.title: bib-photo-ingestion-watcher
@graph.description: Integration-watcher for bib physical-review issues. When a page photo is uploaded to a `bib-physical-review` issue (or an in-repo source passage is agent-identified), OCR/read it, formalise the cited result (if the project has a formal-proof pipeline), confirm the project's usage matches the source, run machine + agent bib validation, then set the reference status to `validated` and refresh references.review.json. Use when processing a bib-physical-review issue that has an attached photo, or when ingesting an uploaded paper.

@graph.name: bib-qa
@graph.title: Bibliography QA Skill
@graph.description: Bibliography quality-assurance agent — validates every reference in content/schema/references.ts against several QA checks: URL availability, URL resolution, metadata completeness, citation coverage, and screenshot/image evidence.  Generates bib-qa.json consumed by the standalone bib-qa.html dashboard.

@graph.name: symbiotic-interaction
@graph.title: symbiotic-interaction — the three registers of author input
@graph.description: Recognize and respond to the three epistemic registers of author input — Socratic steer (known-answer correction), honest gap (flagged unknown), and intuition seed (tenuous cross-domain identification) — with the coactive-learning measurement spec (per-arc correction quality and turns-to-convergence) and the prompt-lexicon convention. Generic folio-assistant platform skill.

@graph.name: block-density
@graph.title: Block Density — Topic Coherence and Table Extraction Skill
@graph.description: Audits individual content blocks for single-topic coherence, length, and embedded tables.  Blocks that cover multiple topics or exceed ~2/3 of a page should be split; large tables (>5 rows) must be their own `table` block.  Child blocks from a split may belong in different chapters than the parent.

@graph.name: idle-backlog
@graph.title: idle-backlog
@graph.description: While idle or waiting on a long-running async task (a build, a long compute script, a CI run, a background agent), pull the applicable backlog in priority order and work non-conflicting items instead of stalling. Generalises AGENTS.md's 5-minute idle trigger into a reusable skill. Use whenever blocked on an async wait with no substantive output to produce.

@graph.name: pending-show
@graph.title: /pending-show — what is this session working on?
@graph.description: Show the current session's pending work — beans list + ledger intent. Read-only.

@graph.name: prepare-merge-auto
@graph.title: /prepare-merge-auto — Autonomous merge pipeline
@graph.description: Full autonomous prepare-merge → resolve → merge pipeline. Coordinates with sibling PRs, resolves review comments, asks structured questions only when blocked, then merges.

@graph.name: integration-backlog
@graph.title: /integration-backlog — drive the backlog to zero, one PR at a time
@graph.description: Dispatcher for the `/integration-backlog <axes>` slash command. Works the backlog identified by the integration watchers (proof, canonical, compute, detangler, one-voice, …) by clustering the open findings into review-sized batches (≤ 49 files per PR — the reviewer-bot limit), proposing each batch to the author via structured AskUserQuestion calls, running `/prepare-merge` on each, resolving review comments (auto if mechanical, structured AskUserQuestion if architectural), then merging — and repeating until the axis is exhausted or the author signals stop. Sister command to `/integration-watch`: the watcher MONITORS for new events; this skill WORKS the backlog the watcher already catalogued.

@graph.name: bean-blocking
@graph.title: Blocking is a claim about the work, not a mood
@graph.description: Default to non-blocking when updating a bean's status. Mark blocked only when the work genuinely cannot proceed, and then always with what it waits on, when the wait expires, and what the next agent should do.

@graph.name: exposition-swarm-drain
@graph.title: /exposition-swarm-drain — Milnor-exposition audit→resolve drain
@graph.description: Drain the paper's narrative blocks through an exposition-quality swarm: a small fleet of grouped-batch agents each audit their batch against the Milnor exposition gate (expo-milnor-clarity, H1–H8) plus the deterministic narrative defect checks (proof-sketch-vs-kind, proof-no-lean-mention-in-prose, proof-cross-block-duplication), then RESOLVE the flagged blocks with conservative, math-preserving edits. Each swarm agent owns its own branch (commits, pushes, opens a PR); the foreground session runs auto prepare-merge on each swarm branch and repeats batch-by-batch until the paper is completely drained. Sister to `/integration-backlog` (that drains watcher findings; this drains exposition quality).

@graph.name: integration-watcher
@graph.title: integration-watcher (abstract parent)
@graph.description: Abstract parent skill for domain-specific **integration watchers**. Encodes the shared mechanics — Monitor on `origin/main`, PR subscriptions, per-event QA dispatch, queue + ledger, idle backlog sweep, idle author-ask dispatcher, watch-PRs-you-prepare protocol, voice-pass on PR diff, witness-drift CI recovery, billing-quick-fail flake handling — that every concrete watcher inherits. Children fill nine domain-specific slots; everything else is shared here.

@graph.name: content-graph
@graph.title: Content Graph — Editorial Organisation Skill
@graph.description: Editorial graph analysis skill — builds a content graph from uses[], interprets, proofs, and examples relationships; builds a chapter/section topology graph; and applies heuristics to identify forward references, cross-section/cross-chapter coupling, and sections that are too sparse or too dense. Produces actionable reorganisation suggestions and can implement approved moves.

@graph.name: one-voice-integration-watcher
@graph.title: /one-voice-integration-watcher
@graph.description: One-voice integration watcher — watches origin/main + open active PRs + newly-opened PRs for content-block changes (`.md`, `.ts`, proof files), runs the per-block QA suite covering scholarly voice, AI-slop detection, section/chapter fit, canonical-vs-deprecated notation usage, and domain-boundary placement. Persists every finding to a sibling `<block>.qa.json` audit report (multi-reviewer, per-field SHA staleness). The watcher NEVER stops — when no events arrive it falls back to idle-sweep of the staleness backlog, rebuilding the audit knowledge base that feeds future content reviews. Inherits shared mechanics (Monitor, subscriptions, queue, ledger, idle sweep, author-ask, watch-prepared-PRs, witness-drift recovery, billing-quick-fail flake, sibling-PR comment protocol) from `local/integration-watcher`.

@graph.name: coordinate
@graph.title: /coordinate — multi-agent / multi-PR coordination
@graph.description: Coordinate work across multiple in-flight Claude PRs working toward a shared goal. Post intent + asks on related PRs, identify cherry-pickable work, respond to code-review comments on your own PR, periodically triage sibling PR activity (new comments, CI status, new commits), watch main + newly created branches/PRs, escalate inconsistent findings to the author, and keep a coordination ledger up to date.

@graph.name: session-intent
@graph.title: /session-intent — durable session intent + results
@graph.description: Session-start intent declaration + session-end results recording, against the goal-scoped master ledger and queue file. Enforces the durable-handoff discipline so any agent can pick up another's thread.

@graph.name: build-docs
@graph.title: /build-docs
@graph.description: Builds the Lean HTML documentation (doc-gen4) locally in the workspace, for any paper folio's Lean package.

@graph.name: latex-build-cache
@graph.title: LaTeX build performance — findings + what's safe
@graph.description: LaTeX build performance — findings + what's safe. The headline goal was to cache a large multi-chapter `report` build (a ~35-chapter / ~2900-block `report` with a heavy `pgf`/`tikz`/`tikz-cd`/`hyperref` preamble + many tikz-cd diagrams). Both standard caching mechanisms were tested on a real engine and FAILED on this toolchain (see §Negative results), so there is currently NO preamble/diagram cache. What DOES work: getting a TeX engine into the sandbox (`scripts/install-tex.sh`) and quick changed-chapter feature builds (`scripts/feature-build.sh`). Read this BEFORE re-attempting a LaTeX cache so you don't re-walk the rakes.

@graph.name: document-intake
@graph.title: Document Intake
@graph.description: Process uploaded documents (PDFs, scans, LaTeX, structured/normative guidelines, etc.) from uploads/ into structured content objects. Handles OCR extraction, environment detection, structural analysis, and content-object generation. Supports multi-stage pipelines: raw upload → extracted text → structured blocks → .ts/.md content objects.

@graph.name: lean-generation
@graph.title: Lean File Generation
@graph.description: Extract theorem-like objects from LaTeX source and generate corresponding Lean 4 stub files with `sorry` placeholders.  Maintains the proof-objects.json manifest linking LaTeX labels to Lean declarations by doc-gen4 URL.

@graph.name: proof-conciseness
@graph.title: Proof Conciseness
@graph.description: Tighten narrative (human-readable) proofs without changing mathematical content. Targets verbose prose patterns in `.md` proof files — padding phrases, re-explained elementary steps, redundant restatement, long case analyses that collapse into tables. Complements proof-simplifier (Lean tactics) and readability-editing (chapter prose); this skill operates on the proof block's `.md` specifically and preserves every logical step.

@graph.name: proposition-consolidation-audit
@graph.title: /proposition-consolidation-audit
@graph.description: Scan a chapter (or the whole paper) for propositions/theorems/lemmas that overlap structurally — same boxed equation under different parametrisations, near-identical proof skeletons, explicit "specialisation of"/"case of"/"corollary of" wording in `.md`, or high-overlap on (uses, cites, tags). Reports candidates for consolidation: parent → corollary, true duplicates, mergeable statements. Run after large-scale chapter work or when the user notices the exposition has accreted special cases.

@graph.name: verify-local-substrate
@graph.title: Verify Anchor Connectivity
@graph.description: Verify that every result block of a designated class traces back to a designated anchor definition through the uses[] dependency graph. Identifies gaps where claims lack a formal connection to the anchor, and suggests fixes.

@graph.name: ffi-roundtrip-audit
@graph.title: FFI roundtrip audit
@graph.description: Audit compute scripts for script ↔ native ping-pong patterns — loops that cross the FFI / subprocess boundary per iteration, instead of one boundary crossing for the whole pipeline. Each occurrence forfeits a meaningful fraction of wall time to marshalling + script-side combine overhead. Performance-only — no correctness change.

@graph.name: proof-integration-watcher
@graph.title: /proof-integration-watcher
@graph.description: Proof-QA integration watcher — watches origin/main + open active PRs + newly-opened PRs for narrative-proof (`.md`) or Lean-proof (`.lean`) changes, runs the proof QA skill suite on every detected change, queues gaps, attempts auto-discharge for easy sorries / naked conjectures with provable scaffolding, and escalates the rest to the author. Inherits shared mechanics (Monitor, subscriptions, queue, ledger, idle sweep, author-ask, watch-prepared-PRs, witness-drift recovery, billing-quick-fail flake, post-completion one-voice, sibling-PR comment protocol) from `local/integration-watcher`.

@graph.name: critical-path-analysis
@graph.title: Critical Path Analysis & Context Review
@graph.description: Analyse the critical path of the paper's argument chain, audit statement and proof contexts (e.g. general vs specialised assumptions), identify blocks that need rewriting, and propose cleanups.  Also covers "statement and proof context review" — classifying each result by whether its statement, proof, or both require specialisation assumptions.

@graph.name: proof-gap-audit
@graph.title: Proof Gap Audit
@graph.description: Audit individual proofs and the network of proofs for gaps. Detects intra-proof gaps (unproved assertions, existence without proof, uniqueness asserted but not shown, hand-waving, missing citations) and inter-proof gaps (missing bridging lemmas, broken chains of implication, unstated propositions needed to tie results together).

@graph.name: chapter-analysis
@graph.title: Chapter Analysis & Formalization
@graph.description: Thorough analysis and Lean 4 formalization of a single manuscript chapter. Extracts all narrative definitions/propositions (excluding remarks), identifies missing glossary terms, writes comprehensive Lean stubs using mathlib, and proves limiting-case and structural theorems where possible.

@graph.name: lean-witness-audit
@graph.title: Lean Witness Audit Skill
@graph.description: Audit computation scripts (typically Python) that produce witness statements for Lean formalization. Verify witnesses are complete, self-documenting, use paper notation, link to a content block, and emit Lean-compatible declarations. Detects staleness via script content hash and git commit SHA.

@graph.name: lean-proof-review
@graph.title: Lean Proof Review
@graph.description: Review Lean 4 proofs for correctness, style, and completeness. Tracks review scores from multiple reviewers (human and agentic) in proof-objects.json.  Integrates with the agent-review pipeline.

@graph.name: proof-status-tracking
@graph.title: Proof Status Tracking
@graph.description: Maintain the proof-objects.json manifest tracking formalization status, review records, and LaTeX-to-Lean linkages.  Generate status dashboards and enforce review policies.

@graph.name: semantic-review-scoping
@graph.title: Semantic review scoping
@graph.description: Decide what to review FIRST. Computes which blocks' semantic correctness can actually affect a target theorem, so agent-adjudicated criteria are spent where they matter instead of swept in file order.

@graph.name: rendering-auditor
@graph.title: Rendering Auditor
@graph.description: Multi-pass rendering auditor for content blocks. Validates markdown+TeX syntax, notation consistency, compilation, layout, and visual output across both HTML and PDF pipelines. Used by author agents after edits and as part of QC reports.

@graph.name: content-block-review
@graph.title: Content Block Review
@graph.description: Reviews existing content blocks for adherence to all requirements — structural integrity, Lean proof rules, cross-reference consistency, status accuracy, and naming conventions. Flags violations with actionable diagnostics.

@graph.name: lean-substantive-pass
@graph.title: /lean-substantive-pass
@graph.description: Convert abstract `holds : Prop` / `claim : Prop` placeholder Lean stubs into typed sub-claim contexts with manuscript-semantic field names. Three escalation levels: hand-craft per-block (highest fidelity), bulk-script split on numbered sub-claims, and docstring enrichment (extract first-sentence summaries from .md). Use this skill after `local/lean-generation` has created the placeholder stubs and the backlog is structurally closed.

@graph.name: compute-audit
@graph.title: Compute Audit Skill
@graph.description: Audit compute scripts for a catalogue of correctness and performance antipatterns extracted from a long review of the project's compute history. Distinguishes CORRECTNESS antipatterns from PERFORMANCE antipatterns. Produces a ranked workplan citing concrete files+lines.

@graph.name: category-theory
@graph.title: Category Theory Formalization
@graph.description: Category Theory formalization skill — handles diagram chasing, universal properties, functorial translation, and whiskering in Lean 4.  Integrates with Mathlib's typeclass-centric category theory and provides tactic strategies for commutativity proofs.

@graph.name: lean-proof-vacuity-audit
@graph.title: lean-proof-vacuity-audit
@graph.description: Detect and fix Lean "vacuous proof" anti-patterns — declarations that type-check, are sorry-free and axiom-clean, and whose statement matches the .md, yet carry NO mathematical content (they assume what they claim, conclude something trivially true, or rest on a false premise). These slip past `proof-statement-integrity` (which only checks signature-stability + an axiom sweep), so detection is semantic and agent-checked. Use when auditing Lean for circular / vacuous / trivially-true proofs, after a batch proof-statement-integrity normalization (the batch "wrap the conclusion in a structure field and project it" fix produces these), or when a "theorem" looks too easy. Emits per-block QA sidecar params under the `proof-no-*` criteria.

@graph.name: formalizer
@graph.title: Lean 4 Formalizer (Narrative to Proof)
@graph.description: Lean 4 Formalizer — translates the logical skeleton of narrative mathematical proofs into Lean 4 tactic blocks.  Uses the Ontologist's glossary to resolve types, maps narrative proof phrases to Lean tactics, and generates sorry-bridged partial proofs that compile.

@graph.name: proof-narrative-lean-equivalence
@graph.title: Proof Narrative ↔ Lean Equivalence Audit
@graph.description: For each content block with both a narrative proof (.md) and a Lean sibling (.lean), verify the two prove the same thing. Detect stub-weakening (Lean claims less than the paper), overreach (Lean claims more than the paper), hypothesis mismatches, and notation drift. Produces a structured equivalence report; no edits.

@graph.name: compute-author
@graph.title: Compute-author skill — read before writing compute code
@graph.description: Pre-work briefing + durable patterns for anyone writing or modifying compute scripts (or the native crates they call). Read this BEFORE you write or change compute code — it covers precision discipline, the native↔script boundary cost, exact-arithmetic choices (big-integer vs big-rational vs arbitrary-precision float), algebraic-preflight requirements before optimization shortcuts, and witness-emission discipline. Sibling to `compute-audit` (post-hoc); this skill is pre-work.

@graph.name: q-usage-watcher
@graph.title: /q-usage-watcher
@graph.description: q-usage integration watcher — detects how each content block treats the substrate parameter $q$ (symbolic / generic-R / real-positive / q > 1 / |q| > 1 / unit-circle / root-of-unity / fixed q_0 / n/a) and cross-checks the detected regime vector against the chapter's narrative-expected profile. Emits per-block `<block>.qa.json` sidecars under the `q-usage-*` criteria and a global witness JSON. Inherits shared mechanics (Monitor, subscriptions, queue, ledger, idle sweep, author-ask, watch-prepared-PRs, witness-drift recovery, billing-quick-fail flake) from `local/integration-watcher`.

@graph.name: remark-audit
@graph.title: Remark Audit Skill
@graph.description: Audit remarks for provable content. Every remark must interpret a mathematical statement that can be formalized in Lean. Detects dangling remarks (no `interprets` link), ambiguous domain terms, and missing formalization.

@graph.name: paper-importer
@graph.title: Paper Importer
@graph.description: Import external papers from PDF, LaTeX, or arXiv into the content object system. Scans for theorems, definitions, propositions, lemmas, and other formal environments. Generates .ts manifests and .md content files, optionally creates .lean stubs with sorry-bridged proofs citing the original source. Integrates with proof-writer skills so imported theorems can inform and accelerate formalization of the main paper.

@graph.name: lean-formal-graph
@graph.title: Lean formal dependency graph
@graph.description: Build and query the FORMAL dependency graph — what a proof actually invokes, derived from `lean.ref`. Distinct from `uses[]`, which is editorial. Use for impact analysis, exposition gaps, and declaration ownership.

@graph.name: proof-editor
@graph.title: Proof Editor (Coordinator)
@graph.description: Coordinator skill for proof review and repair. Runs the full proof skill suite (gap audit, lean review, completeness, simplifier, triage), deduplicates findings across reviewers, ranks by severity and dependency order, and delivers a single author-ready action plan with concrete suggested edits (never applying them without author approval).

@graph.name: lean-environment-setup
@graph.title: Lean Environment Setup
@graph.description: Sets up and troubleshoots the Lean 4 environment for Claude Code sessions. Ensures elan, lake, lean are installed so the paper-assistant MCP's Lean tools are operational. Handles sandboxed/cloud environments where downloads may be restricted.

@graph.name: proof-exposition-review
@graph.title: Proof Exposition Review
@graph.description: Paper-wide retrospective review of a single proof block. Given the current state of the paper — including all blocks added since the proof was written — suggest simplifications to the statement, proof, or surrounding exposition. Complements proof-simplifier (which operates on 2-4 block local clusters) by considering the full dependency graph and all recently-added content.

@graph.name: lean-mathlibext-curator
@graph.title: `MathlibExt` Curator Skill
@graph.description: Curate `<Paper>/MathlibExt.lean` — the staging area for upstream- candidate lemmas (List/sort plumbing, Foldl/foldr at Monoid level, Real-function bridges).  Decide what lives in `MathlibExt` vs inline, and tag candidates with `-- TODO upstream: …`.

@graph.name: lean-completeness-audit
@graph.title: Lean Completeness Audit Skill
@graph.description: Audit Lean formalization completeness across all papers: verify Lake project setup, check import coverage, identify missing .lean files for content blocks that require them, report formalization gaps, and detect stale witnesses.

@graph.name: build-pdf
@graph.title: /build-pdf

@graph.name: lean-cache-restore
@graph.title: Lean cache: the authoring loop
@graph.description: The Lean build loop — restore a warm cache before working, and contribute your build back when done. One command each. A restore is ~2 minutes; a cold Mathlib build is 30-60.

@graph.name: groebner-basis
@graph.title: Gröbner Basis Skill
@graph.description: Compute Gröbner bases and normal forms for (possibly non-commutative) algebraic structures using a CAS (e.g. Singular letterplace) or an instrumented project routine. Reduce words to normal form with step-by-step logging, extract invariants, and emit witness JSON.

@graph.name: lean-build-fix
@graph.title: Lean Build Fix Skill
@graph.description: Iteratively fix Lean build errors and linter warnings until the build passes cleanly. Uses MCP diagnostics when available, falls back to parsing lake build output.

@graph.name: definition-clarity-audit
@graph.title: definition-clarity-audit
@graph.description: Definition / statement clarity + concision audit. A content block can validate (schema-clean, refs resolve, formal-proof sibling present) and still read badly: the defined term is never emphasised, the definition is buried under paragraphs of motivation, or one `definition` block silently bundles three or four distinct definienda. No existing QA axis (voice / structure / bib / proof / …) measures clarity of the statement itself. Use when asked to "bold defined terms", "tighten definitions", "no rambling definitions", "one definition per block", "tight theorem/proposition/lemma statements", or to set up / run a clarity audit. Also runs the inverse audit — a non-`definition` block that secretly carries a definition (`clarity-defn-misplaced`) — plus a statement-purity check (`clarity-stmt-pure`: a theorem/prop/lemma/conjecture carries only its claim; embedded remark / interpretation moves to a follow-on `remark`) and a register check (`clarity-grad-style`: graduate-level formal-math prose — no contractions, second-person, hype, colloquialism, or emoji). Emits per-block QA sidecar params under the `clarity-*` criteria via `content/pipeline/definition-clarity-audit.ts`.

@graph.name: simulator-math-audit
@graph.title: Simulator Math Audit
@graph.description: Audit simulator content objects against the formal mathematics they visualise — formulas and physical constants must be derived from the paper's canonical sources, never hardcoded in the visualisation.

@graph.name: rendering-fixes
@graph.title: Rendering Fixes
@graph.description: Quick-fix reference for common rendering errors found by the rendering-auditor. Agents should consult this when editing content blocks to avoid introducing issues and to fix flagged problems efficiently.

@graph.name: proof-triage

@graph.name: Docling (layout-aware PDF parsing)
@graph.description: IBM's MIT-licensed document parser: layout analysis, TableFormer table structure, formula enrichment. Stage 3 of docs/proposals/rag-document-ingestion.md §10 — the ~20 documents pypdf cannot serve (7 no-TOC, 17 unsectioned, 7 likely-scanned) plus the WHO L1 guidelines, where boxed recommendations and GRADE tables are layout facts. IMPORTANT: `pip install docling` succeeds but a first parse fetches weights from huggingface.co, which returns `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403` under organisation policy (re-measured 2026-08-26). So the import is NOT the capability, and this probe does not stop there: it passes when the weights are already cached locally, and otherwise falls back to a 5-second reachability check. A sandboxed session therefore reports ABSENT and a workstation with models downloaded passes offline and instantly. Run it where egress allows and commit the artefacts.

@graph.name: PyMuPDF (preferred PDF reader backend for pdf-structure.py)
@graph.description: Optional PDF reader backend for scripts/pdf-structure.py, preferred over pypdf when present. Its text layer is cleaner on math PDFs (fewer split words, correct accents, correct CJK where pypdf yields mojibake), and it reads the embedded outline directly via get_toc() rather than walking pypdf's outline object. pdf-structure.py auto-detects it and falls back to pypdf when absent, so it is never required. LICENCE: PyMuPDF is AGPL-3.0 (or commercial); the shipped Docker image installs pypdf (BSD-3-Clause), not PyMuPDF, so this stays an opt-in accelerator. Install: pip install pymupdf.

@graph.name: Lean Atlas
@graph.description: Extracts the Lean constant-dependency graph, classified into type (statement-level) and value (proof-level) edges — the authoritative source for the formal dependency relation. MIT. Added as a Lake require in the CONTENT repo's lakefile.toml (scope NyxFoundation, https://github.com/NyxFoundation/lean-atlas), not installed as a standalone binary, so `lake update` needs github.com egress. Export with `lake exe atlas graph-data --output graph.json --pretty`, then adapt to JSONL for `content/pipeline/lean-atlas-ingest.ts --ingest`. Requires Lean >= 4.17.0 (v4.28.0 tested); the folio image and CI now pin v4.24.0, matching qou. When unavailable, `lean-atlas-ingest.ts --scan` gives an approximate syntactic fallback and every consumer degrades to n/a rather than a false pass.

@graph.title: FHIR Validation Requirements
@graph.description: FHIR Implementation Guide content must pass SUSHI compilation, IG Publisher QA, and conformance validation.

statements.label: SUSHI compilation succeeds
statements.requirement: All FSH files SHALL compile successfully with SUSHI before IG Publisher build.

statements.label: IG Publisher QA passes
statements.requirement: The IG Publisher build SHALL complete with no errors in qa.html.

statements.label: CRMI profile conformance
statements.requirement: Resources SHOULD conform to CRMI profiles (Shareable, Publishable, Computable, Executable) as applicable.

statements.label: Terminology bindings valid
statements.requirement: All terminology bindings SHALL reference valid ValueSets with resolvable codes.

@graph.title: Commit Hygiene
@graph.description: All commits must be clean: no build artifacts, no secrets, pinned dependencies.

statements.label: No build artifacts in commits
statements.requirement: Commits SHALL NOT include generated build artifacts (dist/, node_modules/, *.class, etc.).

statements.label: No secrets in commits
statements.requirement: Commits SHALL NOT include secrets, API keys, tokens, or credentials.

statements.label: Pin dependency versions
statements.requirement: All dependency versions SHALL be pinned or locked (package-lock.json, requirements.txt with versions).

@graph.title: Lean Proof Verification Requirements
@graph.description: Formal mathematics content must have verified Lean 4 proofs with proper sorry tracking.

statements.label: Lean project compiles
statements.requirement: The Lean 4 project SHALL compile with `lake build` without errors.

statements.label: Sorry annotations tracked
statements.requirement: All `sorry` placeholders SHALL be annotated with reference to the corresponding proof obligation.

statements.label: Citations match bibliography
statements.requirement: All citations in LaTeX documents SHALL have corresponding bibliography entries.

@graph.title: Session Start Protocol
@graph.description: Every agent session must detect the user role and check environment capabilities before proceeding.

statements.label: Detect user role
statements.requirement: The agent MUST determine the user's role at session start by checking identity sources against the role assignment table.

statements.label: Check environment capabilities
statements.requirement: The agent MUST probe for all capabilities referenced by skills the user's role can access.

statements.label: Check open todos
statements.requirement: The agent SHOULD check for open todos and present a summary to the user.

@graph.title: Content Development Lifecycle
@graph.description: Content must follow the plan → author → validate → review → test → publish → feedback lifecycle with appropriate phase gates.

statements.label: Planning precedes authoring
statements.requirement: Content authoring MUST NOT begin until a project plan with defined scope and team is established.

statements.label: Validation precedes review
statements.requirement: Content MUST pass automated validation (schema, FHIR, Lean) before entering formal review.

statements.label: Review precedes testing
statements.requirement: Content MUST receive formal review approval before integration testing.

statements.label: Testing precedes publication
statements.requirement: Content MUST pass all tests before publication.

statements.label: Publication requires authorization
statements.requirement: Publication MUST be authorized by the Programme Manager or designated authority.

statements.label: Feedback collected post-publication
statements.requirement: Feedback SHOULD be collected from implementers and users after publication and triaged for the next iteration.
